My argument against the swastika isn't that it scares normies, or that it's too much of a historical burden or anything else. I think that angle of argument fundamentally misses the main point.

The swastika isn't ours. It doesn't belong to us. It is the symbol of a people that bravely joined together and stood against the entire world, fought against impossible odds in order to stop the emerging globalist world order and to protect the people they loved from the chaos that has ensued since. But it is the symbol of another people in another time and another place.

You want to be like the great fash leaders of yesteryear ? Then why use that symbol ? Hitler didn't use the flag of the German Empire because he mourned its loss, and he certainly didn't use the flag of the French Royalty (a foreign and formerly enemy power) because he hated the outcome of the French Revolution. Can you imagine ? Can you fucking imagine Hitler trying to organize a rally in Germany with dudes flying the emblem of the bourbon royals ? Hitler, and every one of those great European leaders created new symbols to represent their movement because they wanted something that represented THEM. The symbols they chose were symbols that gave meaning to their people at the time and place they were living in. Nationalist symbols have to be unique to the people who are creating them. You don't fucking copy the symbols of other nations, no matter how much you revere and respect them. I love the aesthetic. I have all kinds of artwork and photos and videos because the aesthetics of everything those guys did was on point. They turned a marching band into a semi-religious experience. When with like-minded people, I'll share some of it and talk more openly about it. Normies don't like it not just because it's "spooky" because they instinctively know it isn't a symbol that represents them. Even if they're on board with the ideology they know it's the symbol of another group of people from another time that very likely their family members fought and even died fighting, right or wrong. We acknowledge humans are tribal. So why are we flying the banner of a different tribe, even if it is the banner of a brother tribe we were tricked into fighting ? I'm NatSoc and even I can't imagine myself ever showing up to a march and publicly LARPing. Even look at the somewhat more successful NatSoc(ish) groups in modern times. TradWorkersParty and NordFront both invented new symbols because that is what you do. How's the American Nazi Party doing ? Does anyone even fucking know ? Does anyone even care ? No because these guys show up pretending that they belong to a movement that died in a country they've never been to decades before they were even born. And I respect and understand the reasons why they do it, but we have to move on.

So the question is, what do we DO about the so-called swastika question ? Jonathan Bowden was fundamentally right in his response to all this shit, and it goes beyond the swastika question. We need to step over it. When you step over something, it means you don't even bother with it anymore and move past it to something new and better. Because we are going to win, and we're going to build something great of our own. We won't have to look back to fleeting glimmers of hope from the past. But we can't do that if we won't step over it. We continue to cling to the past because I fundamentally think most of us don't think we have any chance of winning, and so we cling to our romantic fatalism and pretend we're the last soldiers standing guard over a dead movement. There are a whole bunch of topics this applies to as well. You know why we're making headway so well ? Is it because of Ernst Zundel's work on holocaust revisionism ? No. It's because nobody gives a shit anymore and the younger generation thinks this shit is funny. Step over it. If someone starts blathering on about the ebil nazis and da hallofcost nine times out of ten the correct response isn't to show them graphs and statistics, it's to laugh at them and tell them no one cares anymore. Step. over. it. If the person seems like the type to be open minded to new information, sure, show them your info. But again, the correct response in the majority of cases is to just say 'Well I don't care about that, here's what I care about'.

We need new symbols, symbols that represent us and our people and the situation we are fighting in. We need real victories and things that we can be proud of. If you want to get rid of the LARPers, give these people something in the here and now that they can be proud of and can be a part of. Because that is fundamentally what these people want. They want something to dedicate themselves to. They want something heroic to be a part of. These people have the capacity for great bravery and strength but are stuck clinging to the exploits of foreign heroes in past ages because they don't see anything in the here and now.

And if that doesn't work do the literal opposite. If you can't step into those shoes and inspire people to take on the symbol of a new movement then have every single person at these marches waving a nazi flag. Take the /pol/ route and just embrace the absurdity. Because if you have even one nazi flag at your rally you might as well have a thousand. In the eyes of the media the two are equivalent. And frankly, the optics are better. One nazi flag makes it look like the march is just a bunch of pathetic isolated LARPers. A thousand and it looks like this is a real thing happening.
